name: Red Sea saline overflow - southern plume reference reach
scope: Declared southern descending-plume regional connection from an OSW Bab-el-Mandeb approach gate toward the Figure 1 lower-channel neighborhood. Every vertex is an independent rounded editorial choice. Excludes the other branch, gully products, late equilibrated-water spreading and a whole-parent length.
layer: Descending dense Red Sea outflow plume branch, with bottom and interfacial layers and changing equilibrium depth. Not a surface flow, fixed 100-250 m depth slab, channel width or equilibrated-water boundary undercurrent.
time_convention: REDSOX winter/summer 2001 geographic branch context; selected path is editorial, not a synoptic velocity axis or reconstructed seasonal routes. Cruises and station composites are separate occupations.
source_locator: Peters et al. (2005), section 2, section 3a and Figure 1 printed571 / PDF3 identify two preferred descending plume pathways. Section5a printed575 / PDF7 describes non-synoptic velocity-supported northern reach 130 km; channel lengths / 5 km width are different objects. Source figure inspected for orientation only.
source_citation: Peters, Johns, Bower and Fratantoni (2005), Mixing and Entrainment in the Red Sea Outflow Plume. Part I: Plume Structure, Journal of Physical Oceanography 35, 569-583.
source_license: Copyright 2005 American Meteorological Society. Original retained locally and ignored; independently selected OSW vertices and attributed facts only. No source figure or bathymetric curve copied.
coordinate_selection: Source supports the declared regional geography or study-domain convention. OSW selects all gates, rounded connecting vertices and alternative bends; no velocity axis or source trajectory reconstructed. Independent longitude and endpoint-latitude shifts describe drawing choices, not current width, source position errors or seasonal extrema.
